reason: E1 states that substrate heating is a strategy to mitigate thermal stresses and hot cracking in HEAs, supporting the general premise. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides specific evidence on AlCrFeNiSi, the 300°C temperature, or the claimed 15–20% mechanical improvement; E2 discusses in situ heating benefits in tool steels and DED but not this HEA system. Thus, the key premises are only partly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Substrate preheating reduces thermal gradients in AM of HEAs
Reduced thermal gradients minimize segregation and residual stress
Reduced defects and residual stress improve mechanical integrity
The effect applies to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder in LPBF/DED
A preheat of ~300°C is sufficient to achieve ~15–20% improvement
